status: proposal, awaiting Chanté's approval. Nothing here is canonical until approved; close-up assets are not generated. v3 (2026-09-13) is measured on art/scenery/library/background.png, Chanté's isometric repaint of the room, which answers the map's question 3 (the Library shares the isometric projection of bet 5). It is a new measurement, not a camera view of the frontal painting v1 and v2 were drawn on: every coordinate changed. The slots, their numbering and the questions carry over.
about: The Library's camera-view manifest. Stable spatial IDs name physical places only; what a slot holds for a user (a Collection's name, a Thread Group's name) is data stored elsewhere, never here. The annotated maps in spatial-map/ are drawn from this file by scripts/draw-library-map.py, so edit the numbers here and redraw.

coordinates.convention: Normalized to the canonical wide painting: x 0.0 (left) to 1.0 (right), y 0.0 (top) to 1.0 (bottom). Rectangles are {x, y, w, h}; polygons are lists of [x, y]. For Lumi a point is where her feet touch the floor or a surface.
coordinates.faces: Every bookcase stands on a wall, and a wall is a flat face: `face` gives its top-left, top-right and bottom-left corners (vertical edges stay vertical in this projection; horizontal edges slant with the wall). Everything on a bookcase (its plaque, text-safe zone and Thread Group rows) is in that face's own coordinates {u, v, w, h}, 0..1 across and down the face, so a point is tl + u*(tr - tl) + v*(bl - tl). The centre bay's face is a plain rectangle; the side walls' faces are parallelograms.
coordinates.closeup_projection: A close-up's `frame` is a region in its slot's face coordinates (it may reach past 0..1 to take in the neighbours). With `rectify: affine` the frame is un-sheared into a 2:3 rectangle, and the side walls' foreshortening is undone by widening it by `projection.side_wall_widening`: in a parallel projection that is exact, so the rectified crop is the reference image for generating the close-up, not a guess at a new camera. The CSS camera move is the same affine map as a matrix() transform of the wide layer. Until a close-up is generated and measured, its geometry is the face geometry; measured close-up coordinates go under `measured` and take precedence.

source.note: An isometric cutaway on a dark ground. The frontal painting v2 was measured on is archived as art/archived/scene_mockups/library-background-frontal.png.

projection.kind: parallel (isometric-like): no vanishing point, so an object is the same size anywhere on the floor
projection.note: The left and right walls slant about 0.4 (screen dy/dx), and so do the floor's edges; the back corner is cut across by a wall facing the camera, which holds the centre bay. Reading the walls as 45 degrees to the picture plane seen from about 24 degrees above, a length along a side wall shows at about 0.71 of its size, so a side-wall close-up is widened by 1.414. The painting has a little perspective (the slope runs 0.35-0.45 across the room), which each face absorbs by being measured on its own.

depth_scale.note: A parallel projection: she is the same size anywhere on the floor. No horizon to estimate, which is what walking in the room needs.

lumi.size_note: At her usual size she is about 0.8 of the doorway under the stair and 1.6-1.8 of an armchair: taking the doorway as about 2 m, a figure about 1.6 m tall. At 0.6 of her size (a 90px box) she is about 1 m, a little taller than an armchair and half the doorway. The furniture now agrees with itself (the circle's and the alcove's armchairs are the same scale), so the question is only her size in the room. stills.png shows her at 1.0, stills-60.png at 0.6.

transitions.scale_to_frame: Acknowledge (the plaque warms, about 150ms). Then transform the wide layer with the frame's affine map (a matrix(): scale, translate and, on a side wall, un-shear) so the frame fills the stage (about 800ms, ease-in-out). Crossfade to the close-up asset over the last 250ms, aligned to the same rectangle. Thread Group plaques and Thread spines fade in after. Lumi may turn toward the slot or start walking; the camera never waits for her.
transitions.pull_out_to_parent: The reverse, back into the wall. Back is a visible control as well as the browser's Back.
transitions.pan_to_thread_group: Inside a close-up: translate vertically so the chosen row sits in the readable band (about 500ms). Not a new view.
transitions.crossfade_via_table: Selecting a Thread ends spatial navigation: the view crossfades to library_table (about 400ms) and the book opens at once. Lumi's retrieval runs alongside and never delays it.
transitions.pull_out_to_origin: From the table, back to the Thread Group row it came from (or library_wide).
transitions.reduced_motion: Every transition becomes a 200ms crossfade; Lumi does not walk.
